edits.old: Hashing tenantId can distribute different tenant values across shards and reduce hotspots from sequentially assigned tenant IDs, but range queries on the hashed field are less efficient. Hashing tenantId alone still gives each tenant one shard-key value, so it cannot split an unusually large tenant by itself. To preserve tenant-based targeting while allowing a large tenant to span ranges, one option is a compound key with tenantId as a prefix and a suffix that varies within the tenant (which may be hashed). A different high-cardinality shard key, such as hashed _id, can also distribute data, but tenant-only queries that omit that key are broadcast across shards. (high confidence)
edits.new: Hashed sharding gives a more even data distribution at the cost of targeted operations: ranged queries on the hashed field are more likely to be broadcast, though equality matches can be targeted to a single shard. Hashing suits monotonically changing values such as ObjectId or timestamps; hashing tenantId alone still gives each tenant one shard-key value (one chunk per value), so it cannot split an unusually large tenant. A compound hashed key with a non-hashed prefix and one hashed field is supported, with the prefix supporting zone ranges and the hashed field giving even distribution. A key that omits the queried field, such as hashed _id, is broadcast for queries that lack the shard key. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/hashed-sharding/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharding-choose-a-shard-key/
